Vincent J. Sodd of the National Center for Radiological Health and James W. Blue of Lewis Research Center describe making iodine-123 in this 1969 memorandum. Iodine-123 had recently been recognized as the most ideal iodine radioisotope for low-exposure measurements inside the body. A cyclotron technique produced it in high purity.

The method bombards antimony-121 with alpha particles, knocking out two neutrons to form iodine-123. The introduction explains the production route. The report record adds procedures for isolating the iodine products. It also covers recovering the enriched target material for reuse. Reliable supply of this isotope supports medical imaging with lower patient radiation exposure.
